[NSTG.2.3.2] **TTL semantics.** `ttl_ns == 0` means no expiry: the
entry lives until an explicit `cache_delete`, and nothing else removes
it. A write that would breach the cache cap fails rather than making
room ([RTCT.7.1]), so a capped cache never evicts to accept a new key.
Non-zero means *expire after this duration*. The engine tracks the deadline for its own cache; a
persistence cb should mirror it into the backing store (set the
store's TTL field, schedule eviction) so a hydrate re-seeds a
consistent view. A hydrate seeds each entry with the lifetime it has left,
which counts from the new engine's first sample ([NLFC.9.4]).
